clues: This city stands on both banks of the Vltava River, in the middle of Europe. Stone bridges cross the river and link its old town parts.
This city sits in the rain shadow of high hills, so less rain falls here than in most of its land. In cold months, fog can hang low for days.
Charles the Fourth was king of Bohemia and a great emperor in the 1300s. He made this city the chief seat of his vast empire.
The famed Charles Bridge, built of stone, crosses the river in this city. It links the old town bank to the bank below the great castle.
The state work of Czechia is run from this city. Its great castle was the home of emperors who ruled a wide realm.
